task: Reconcile the public Salamat Projects Dashboard read-only experiment view with the current canonical Murat Project Engineer experiment registry using the dashboard's existing source/snapshot mechanisms, removing or superseding stale experiment mirror data where necessary without adding write-back, execution controls, runtime services, or deployment changes.
acceptance_criteria: The dashboard experiment view reflects the current canonical MPE experiment statuses and next actions for entries it mirrors, based on current MPE registry/evidence rather than stale open mirror PRs.
Existing read-only architecture and source-adapter/snapshot path are reused; no second registry or competing source of truth is introduced.
No execution controls, write-back to MPE/project repositories, new API/backend/Worker/database, or deployment is added.
Changes are limited to the smallest existing data/source adapter, fixtures/tests, and evidence/docs needed for the reconciliation.
Dashboard validation/tests/build pass and any stale/conflicting open experiment-mirror PRs are identified in evidence rather than silently combined.
No production deployment occurs as part of P-006.
non_scope: No deployment or Cloudflare configuration change.
No project execution controls, Arena/Codex controls, or write-back.
No new repository, service, database, API, or parallel experiment registry.
No unrelated dashboard redesign or portfolio reprioritization.
Do not merge or reuse stale open experiment-mirror PRs without reconciling them against current main and current MPE evidence.

triage_input.summary: Reconcile the public read-only dashboard experiment view with current canonical MPE experiment evidence using existing snapshot/source mechanisms

pre_registered_human_label.rationale: The change is reversible and stays inside the existing read-only dashboard architecture, but it updates public-facing portfolio/experiment status derived from another repository. Source reconciliation and full validation are required to avoid publishing stale or misleading status, so VERIFIED is more appropriate than FAST; no destructive, production-deploy, sensitive-data, permission, or deep-change signal requires owner approval.
